finding: INV-4 / §3 rule 5 VIOLATED (verified by running the real function): spliceTranscript's blank-transcript branch collapses the seam UNCONDITIONALLY, including when the span being removed is ZERO-LENGTH (i.e. nothing was ever written there). The first interim decode commonly returns empty — the design's own §2 measurement shows toolbarCaption=null at t+1.2s — and the engine writes it via writeDictation(session, normalizeInterimTranscript(null)) => spliceTranscript(value, anchor{12,12}, ""). On the design's own repro draft "Please book  for next Tuesday." caret 12, this silently rewrites the user's untouched draft to "Please book for next Tuesday." — one whitespace char destroyed before a single word was dictated. Cancel CANNOT undo it: the session span is now zero-length with anchorText=="", so relocateSpan returns {12,12} and restoreSpan is a no-op, leaving the composer NOT byte-for-byte as it was. Same loss occurs on the interim-shrink path (non-empty write then a blank decode) and persists through a No-speech-detected commit. The collapse is only sound when removing text this session actually wrote; it must be gated on span.end > span.start (or on written !== "").

§5 detach rule + §3 rule 7 VIOLATED: cancelRecording computes restored = dictation.anchor and passes it to focusComposer UNCONDITIONALLY, including when the session DETACHED. restoreDictation() correctly returns early for a detached session ("restores nothing — that text is the user's now"), but focusComposer then still runs store.applyEdit(getText(), anchor.start, anchor.end), SELECTING an arbitrary range of the user's own text at the pre-recording offsets. Reachable state: caret/selection anchor {5,8} on "call Bob tomorrow", interims replace it, the user edits inside the provisional span (detach), then Cancel — the composer ends focused with 3 characters of the USER's text selected, and the next keystroke deletes them. Data-destructive. TEST-16's detach case asserts only textarea.value and never selectionStart/End, so it is green on this.

HOLLOW ACCEPTANCE TEST for INV-5. TEST-19 manufactures the no-caret state with Object.defineProperty(el,'selectionStart',{get:()=>null}) — a value a mounted <textarea> NEVER returns (verified in Chromium: a never-focused textarea whose value was set via el.value=draft, exactly what TextInput's draft-restore effect does, reports selectionStart === value.length; only a textarea whose content came from markup reports 0). Production readSelection() therefore never yields null for a mounted composer, so the entire selection===null branch (insertTranscript's append path, resolveWriteSpan's `?? {value.length,value.length}`, currentCaret's `??`, the anchorText ternary) is unreachable in shipped code, and the REAL never-focused path is not exercised by any test. If the genuine no-caret behaviour regressed (e.g. readSelection started returning {0,0} explicitly, putting dictation at the FRONT of the draft) TEST-19 would still pass. Its companion unit acceptance TEST-6 (voiceLogic.test.ts:~228) has the same defect: it pins a pure-function input production cannot produce.

§3 rule 5 ("the original caret/selection restored") half-implemented on the shifted-span path: restoreDictation relocates the span and applies the CORRECT restored selection via applyEdit(edit.value, edit.start, edit.end), and focusComposer then immediately OVERWRITES it with the STALE anchor offsets. Reachable: user has "Bob" selected at {5,8}, dictation replaces it, the user types "XY" at position 0 during recording (shifting everything by 2), then cancels — the value is restored byte-for-byte but the re-selection lands on {5,8} instead of {7,10}, selecting the wrong three characters. focusComposer should re-select what restoreDictation actually restored, not the anchor. TEST-14/TEST-21 never type before the span, so both are green.

INV-1's "NO transcript text is rendered in the composer toolbar" clause is certified only by assertions that cannot fail. (a) expect(byTestId(page,'voice-live-caption')).toHaveCount(0) is a tautology — the element was deleted from source, so no implementation of this feature could ever make it non-zero; it is repeated 4x across the 14-voice specs. (b) The toolbar text assertion uses page.locator('[data-testid="chat-input-toolbar"], [role="group"]'): `chat-input-toolbar` does not exist anywhere in the repo (grepped), and the only [role="group"] in this flow is MicButton's recording chrome, which is UNMOUNTED by the time the assertion runs (after stopDictation). allInnerTexts() on an empty match set yields [] and join(' ') yields '', so not.toContain('a table') passes vacuously. A regression that re-rendered the transcript in the toolbar WHILE recording would not be caught. Assert the toolbar's text mid-recording against a real, existing container.

§3 framing "Dictation is an editor input" is not honoured by the persistence layer: applyComposerEdit (and setMessage) write el.value directly and dispatch no input/change event, and setDraft() is called ONLY from TextInput.handleInput (onChange, TextInput.tsx:119). Dictated text therefore never enters the draft store. Because this change makes dictation the composer's primary content producer (a per-second stream plus the whole final transcript) rather than one append at Stop, the consequence is now material: dictate, then switch conversation A->B->A and TextInput's restore effect writes the STALE stored draft back over the textarea — the entire transcript is silently lost. Either dispatch a native input event after applyComposerEdit or call setDraft from the applier.

Cross-pane corruption escalated by the offset-based rewrite: ownerTextStore(paneId) silently falls back to Chat.$.TextStore — the FOCUSED pane — when paneRegistry.get(paneId) is undefined, and unregisterPane() deletes the handle on pane unmount (chatBridge.ts:38). An interim tick (~1s timer) or a restoreDictation firing after the recording pane closes therefore applies ABSOLUTE offsets computed against pane A's draft to pane B's composer: spliceTranscript/restoreSpan will delete or overwrite an arbitrary [start,end) range of another conversation's draft. Pre-change the same fallback only appended a stray transcript; it can now destroy text. Resolve the owning store once and BAIL (rather than falling back) when the owning pane is gone.

§3 rule 7 ("the user's own typing always wins") is implemented only for SPAN ownership, not for CARET ownership. writeDictation calls store.applyEdit(edit.value, edit.caret) on EVERY interim tick, unconditionally moving the composer's caret to the end of the dictated words even when the user's caret is elsewhere and they are actively typing. Reachable state ("the user typing during dictation"): with live captions on, a user editing at position 3 while dictation writes at position 50 has their caret yanked ~once per second, so their subsequent keystrokes land INSIDE the dictated span — which then trips relocateSpan into detaching. Rule 7 requires the write to leave the caret alone when the current selection is outside the span being rewritten.

INV-2 ("real time transcribe") is gated behind a control whose user-facing name now describes a surface this change DELETED. The toggle's tooltip and aria-label are still "Turn live captions on/off" and the store field is still liveCaptions, but with the toolbar caption strip removed the switch's only remaining effect is whether dictation streams into the chat input at all. A user who has (or turns) it off gets no real-time transcription and no way to discover that from the label. Rename the affordance (and ideally the state field) to what it now controls, e.g. "Live dictation".

§5 mechanism divergence between the captions-ON and captions-OFF paths: with live captions off the session never writes, so session.span stays null and commitTranscript skips the session entirely, inserting at store.getSelection() (the caret at STOP time) rather than at session.anchor (the caret at RECORD time) that §5 specifies as the first write target. Defensible under rule 7 and documented in the function's own docstring, but it means the same feature has two different insertion-point semantics depending on a preference toggle, and only the captions-OFF one is covered (TEST-15 case 2 never moves the caret during recording, so the two are indistinguishable there).

Behaviour outside the design's stated contract, untested: fail() now calls restoreDictation()+endDictation(), so a transcription FAILURE after interims silently deletes the words the user watched appear. INV-4 enumerates cancelled / superseded / unmounted — not failed; §3 rule 5 likewise. Discarding a recording's visible output on a backend error is a real user-data decision (the audio is gone, the words are gone) that no rule in the design authorises and no test in TESTS.md exercises (no spec drives a /transcribe error after interim writes). Either record it as a decision in the design doc or keep the provisional words and surface the error alongside them.

cancelRecording re-selects the STALE anchor. restoreDictation() (line 236-244) already applies the CORRECT restored span via applyEdit(edit.value, edit.start, edit.end); cancelRecording then sets `restored = dictation.anchor` (the offsets captured at record START) and focusComposer (line 735) re-applies applyEdit(getText(), anchor.start, anchor.end) in a rAF, overwriting the correct selection with stale offsets. REPRODUCED: draft 'call Bob tomorrow' with 'Bob' selected (5..8), interim writes 'Alice Smith', user then types 'AB' at index 0, cancel -> value correctly 'ABcall Bob tomorrow' but the selection is 5..8 = 'l B' instead of 7..10 = 'Bob'. Violates the documented INV-4 'cancel leaves the composer exactly as it was'. TEST-14 in DictationComposer.test.tsx and TEST-21 in dictation-caret-insert.spec.ts both only exercise the no-shift case, so neither catches it. Fix: return the span restoreDictation actually restored instead of dictation.anchor (or drop the redundant re-apply in focusComposer).

ownerTextStore() silently falls back to `Chat.$.TextStore` (the FOCUSED pane) whenever paneRegistry.get(paneId) misses. Before this change that fallback was consulted ONCE, at final commit; the dictation session now calls it on EVERY interim tick, on restoreDictation and on commitTranscript. REPRODUCED with two composers (pane A recording, pane B focused): unregistering pane A mid-recording leaves A's provisional words 'hello there' permanently STRANDED (cancel restores nothing because relocateSpan fails against B's text -> the session silently detaches), and Stop writes the authoritative 'FINAL TRANSCRIPT' into PANE B's composer at PANE B's caret. That is a cross-pane write of dictated content plus an INV-4 violation. A missing owning pane should abort the write, not redirect it to whichever pane happens to be focused.

spliceTranscript's blank-transcript branch runs its seam-collapse even when the span is COLLAPSED (start === end), so a write that removes nothing still DELETES one of the user's characters. REPRODUCED end-to-end: draft 'hello  world' with the caret at 6 (between the two spaces), live captions on, one interim decode returning '' -> composer becomes 'hello world'; cancelRecording does NOT put the space back (restoreDictation relocates the zero-length span and restores the empty anchorText), so INV-4 'byte-exact restore' is false. Guard the collapse on start !== end (nothing was removed => nothing to collapse). The unit suite tests the blank branch only with a NON-empty span (voiceLogic.test.ts:83), so it passes.

focusComposer defers a frame and then re-reads the store, with no epoch/generation check. REPRODUCED: after stopRecording commits the transcript, replacing the composer value before the rAF fires (the conversation-switch case -- TextInput is REUSED across an in-app A->B switch and its draft-restore effect writes el.value directly) leaves the rAF applying the STALE caret offset (19) into the NEW draft and focusing it. The value itself is not clobbered (it re-writes store.getText()), so the harm is a wrong caret plus an unrequested focus steal into a different conversation's composer. It is also reachable from the MicButton unmount cleanup (MicButton.tsx:69-73), which calls cancelRecording -> focusComposer while the component is going away.

The harness comment 'A fresh engine per test: voiceEngine memoizes on the get identity, so a new get closure yields a new engine with clean module-scope session state' is FALSE. dictation, requestGeneration, mediaRecorder, chunks, finalizing, and every timer are MODULE scope in _engine.ts, shared by all engine instances; only errorRevertTimer is per-instance. REPRODUCED: engine A recording, then a second engine built exactly as beforeEach builds it -> B's startRecording overwrites A's `dictation` with no restore, so A's streamed words are stranded and B's cancel restores only B's span. The tests currently pass only because afterEach's cancelRecording tears the shared state down; the comment will mislead the next author into assuming isolation that does not exist.

Vacuous assertion. `page.locator('[data-testid="chat-input-toolbar"], [role="group"]').allInnerTexts()` -- the testid `chat-input-toolbar` does not exist ANYWHERE in the repo (verified by grep over src/ and sdk/), and the only relevant [role="group"] is MicButton's recording wrapper, which is unmounted by the time this runs (after Stop). An empty locator yields [], so `[].join(' ')` is '' and `not.toContain('a table')` passes unconditionally. The prose 'NOTHING transcript-shaped is rendered in the composer toolbar' is therefore unverified by this spec.

The diff replaces a `voice-live-caption` count-0 assertion with `expect(byTestId(page,'chat-message-textarea')).toHaveValue('')` under the comment '...and nothing dictation-shaped reached the composer either'. The test is the UNPERMITTED-user case: it never types, never records, and no mic affordance exists, so the composer is empty for reasons unrelated to dictation. Trivially true; would pass with the whole feature reverted.

`expect(byTestId(page,'voice-live-caption')).toHaveCount(0)` (also at dictation-caret-insert.spec.ts:113 and live-captions-stream.spec.ts:76,82) asserts the absence of an element this same diff DELETED from MicButton.tsx. It can never fail again and is not a guard against a transcript re-appearing in the toolbar -- any future toolbar transcript would use a different element. A meaningful guard would assert on the toolbar's rendered text, which the one spec that tries (dictation-caret-insert.spec.ts:114) does vacuously.

Composer spans are raw UTF-16 code-unit offsets with no surrogate-pair guard, so an offset landing inside a surrogate pair splits the code point. REPRODUCED: spliceTranscript('a\u{1F44D}b', {start:1,end:2}, 'X') -> 'a X \udc4db' (a lone low surrogate, rendered as a replacement glyph); spliceTranscript with a caret at index 2 (inside the pair) -> 'a\ud83d X \udc4db'. Not obviously reachable through the UI (browsers clamp mouse/keyboard selection to code-point boundaries), but applyComposerEdit's setSelectionRange does no such clamping, so an arithmetic caret could produce one. Low, defensive.

clampIndex maps NaN/Infinity/-Infinity to `value.length`, i.e. a corrupt or unreadable selection silently degrades to APPEND-AT-END -- the exact behaviour this feature exists to eliminate -- with nothing logged. Verified: spliceTranscript('abc',{start:NaN,end:NaN},'X') === spliceTranscript('abc',{start:Infinity,...}) === 'abc X'. Repo rule 6 (never silently swallow a real failure) argues for distinguishing 'no insertion point' (the legitimate null case, already modelled) from 'a garbage insertion point'.

applyComposerEdit (and setMessage) write el.value directly and never dispatch an input/change event, so TextInput's onChange handler (handleInput -> setDraft, TextInput.tsx:117-120) never runs for dictated text. A dictated transcript is therefore NEVER persisted to the per-conversation draft, and TextInput's draft-restore effect (TextInput.tsx:112, `el.value = getDraft(draftKey)`) silently overwrites it on the next conversation switch. Pre-existing in class for the old setText-based append, but this change routes far more text (every interim tick plus the final commit) through the same unpersisted path.

fail() unconditionally restores + clears the module-scope `dictation`, but ONE fail() call site runs BEFORE the exclusive recording lock is acquired: startRecording's `if (!isRecordingSupported()) { fail(...) }` at line 461-464 sits above acquireRecordingLock at 469. On that path a live session belonging to ANOTHER pane would be restored (wiping its streamed words) and cleared. Latent only because isRecordingSupported() is a static per-browser predicate that cannot be false for one pane and true for another; still, fail()'s session cleanup should be conditional on this pane owning the session (e.g. dictation.gen === this request's gen, or recordingPaneId match).

acquireRecordingLock(null) returns true UNCONDITIONALLY ('single-pane: no cross-pane exclusion needed'), so a startRecording() with paneId === null bypasses exclusion entirely even while another pane holds the lock -- and then overwrites the module-scope `dictation`, mediaRecorder, chunks and timers of that in-flight recording. The invariant the DictationSession doc-comment relies on ('the exclusive recording lock guarantees at most one pane is in the recording flow at a time') therefore has a hole. Latent because MicButton only passes null when it renders outside a ChatPaneContext, which does not co-occur with split panes today.

focusComposer's guard was narrowed from `typeof document === 'undefined' || typeof requestAnimationFrame === 'undefined'` to just the rAF check, and on that branch it returns having done NOTHING -- no focus and, more importantly, no caret/selection restore. In any environment without rAF the post-stop caret placement and the post-cancel re-selection are silently skipped with no synchronous fallback. Cheap fix: fall back to calling the body inline instead of returning.

The new `el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', {bubbles:true}))` is a NO-OP: it never reaches React's onChange, so the draft-save it exists to trigger still never runs and the silent-data-loss defect its own comment describes is NOT closed. Cause: line 71 still assigns `el.value = text` directly, which goes THROUGH React's per-instance value tracker and updates it; when the input event then fires, React's updateValueIfChanged sees tracker === current and suppresses the synthetic change event. Reproduced on jsdom + the repo's React 19.2.6: assign+dispatch => 0 onChange calls; prototype-setter+dispatch => 1 onChange call with the new value. TextInput wires `onChange={handleInput}` (TextInput.tsx:180), the tracked path, not onInput. This is a fix of the symptom (no event) rather than the cause (the tracker), and it must write through Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLTextAreaElement.prototype,'value').set before dispatching. Corroborated by mutation M6 (deleting the dispatch leaves all 43 unit+component tests green) and by the follow-up commit 9a7c8f9fa, which adds exactly that prototype-setter bypass.

Removing the seam-collapse from spliceTranscript's blank branch fixed the collapsed-caret corruption but OVER-corrected for RANGE anchors, reintroducing a violation of design rule 3.4 ('No doubled spaces'). When the anchor was a SELECTION (dictation replacing selected text) the span removed on a blank decode covers the user's own word, so the two surrounding separators become adjacent. Oracle, running e7c1f2307's voiceLogic.ts against its parent's: 'Hello world beautiful' + select {6,11} + write 'foo' + blank => NEW 'Hello  beautiful' (double space) vs OLD 'Hello beautiful'; 'call Bob tomorrow' + select {5,8} => NEW 'call  tomorrow' vs OLD 'call tomorrow'. Reachable mid-recording on any empty interim decode, and PERSISTENT in the user's draft when the FINAL transcript is empty (announcement 'No speech detected'), because commitTranscript routes an empty final through writeDictation -> the same blank branch. The collapsed-caret fix is correct and must be kept; the tidy should have been made conditional on the removal being pad-only (span.start === span.end at write time / anchorText === '') rather than deleted outright. Note the sibling case 'Say hello, friend' + select {4,9} => 'Say , friend' (space before a comma) is IDENTICAL in both versions, i.e. pre-existing, not a regression of this commit.

commitTranscript may now return undefined because the owning pane closed (line 333), in which case the transcript is deliberately DROPPED - but stopRecording's set() at line 729 still announces `text ? 'Transcript added' : 'No speech detected'`. The screen-reader announcement therefore claims success for a transcript that was discarded, and status flips to idle with no error. This is a new consequence of the null-return introduced by this commit: the drop is silent to assistive tech. The other four ownerTextStore null call sites (focusComposer:172, writeDictation:238, restoreDictation:302, startRecording:616-617) all handle null correctly.

nextSelection compares the user's live selection against `oldSpan`, which is the PRE-normalization span from resolveWriteSpan, while `edit` was computed by spliceTranscript against the CLAMPED/normalized span. When the first write uses a stale anchor captured at record start and the user has since shortened the draft below anchor.start, the clamped insertion happens at value.length while nextSelection still tests against the unclamped anchor, takes the `before.end <= oldSpan.start` branch, and leaves the caret BEFORE the dictated words instead of after them. Bounded: it self-corrects on the next interim tick (the caret is then inside the relocated span), and applyComposerEdit clamps any out-of-range offset, so no invalid offset escapes. Cheap fix: normalize oldSpan once and pass the normalized value to both spliceTranscript and nextSelection.

The commit's headline production change - dispatching a native input event so the dictated transcript is persisted as a draft - ships with ZERO test coverage. Mutation M6 (delete the dispatchEvent line, everything else at e7c1f2307 unchanged) leaves DictationComposer.test.tsx at 16/16 passed and voiceLogic.test.ts at 27/27 passed. No test in this commit can fail if the fix is reverted, which is why the fact that it is also a no-op (see the paired regression row) went undetected. A kill-capable test is cheap here: the component harness already mounts the REAL kit Textarea through the REAL createComposerAccess closures, so a spy on a React onChange handler bound to that textarea would have failed at e7c1f2307 and passed after 9a7c8f9fa.

TEST-19, tagged '[acceptance, INV-5]' and named 'a composer that was never focused still APPENDS at the end', no longer exercises INV-5's no-insertion-point branch at all. The rewritten seeding assigns `el.value = draft`, and per the HTML spec that moves the text entry cursor to the END of the control - verified in jsdom: after `el.value = draft` (len 30) selectionStart === selectionEnd === 30, NOT null. readSelection() therefore returns {30,30}, the engine captures a non-null anchor, and the expected value is produced by the ordinary caret-insert path that merely happens to land at the end. The `?? {start: value.length, end: value.length}` fallbacks (_engine.ts:225 and :356, voiceLogic.ts:182/185) could all be deleted and this test would still pass. The previous version stubbed selectionStart to null and DID cover the branch; this commit removed that coverage without replacing it, so INV-5 now has no e2e test. Same commit also added an unreachable Number.isFinite guard whose only historical trigger was the stub it deleted.

The new toolbarRowText() probe (and its inlined twin in live-captions-stream.spec.ts:85-87) walks up with `while (row && !row.contains(stop)) row = row.parentElement` and has NO upper bound. It cannot pass vacuously today - a missing anchor returns null and the caller asserts not.toBeNull(), and the /0:0\d/ elapsed-timer positive control excludes empty text - but the guard only detects UNDER-scoping. If MicButton ever moves out of the composer's left action group the loop climbs to <html> and returns the whole page's textContent; both not.toContain assertions still pass, because a textarea's live `.value` is not part of textContent, and /0:0\d/ still matches. Related: the helper is mis-named. Its two anchors (chat-input-add-btn and the Stop button) share the LEFT ACTION GROUP (ChatInput.tsx:146), not the toolbar row (ChatInput.tsx:120) that the name and both comments claim, so the toolbar's right group and the toolbar_status row are not covered by this INV-1 assertion. Add a step cap, or assert the located row does not contain the textarea.

ownerTextStore's new null return - documented as preventing a DESTRUCTIVE cross-pane splice ('writing them into a different pane's composer would delete or overwrite an arbitrary range of another conversation's text') - has no test. Mutation M11 (restore the old fallback: `if (!handle) return Chat.$.TextStore`) leaves DictationComposer.test.tsx 16/16 and voiceLogic.test.ts 27/27 green. The component harness stubs paneRegistry.get to always return undefined and every test drives paneId === null, so the pane-registry branch this fix guards is never entered. A change justified on data-integrity grounds should ship with a test that drives paneId to a registered-then-unregistered pane.

Both Number.isFinite guards added to composerAccess in this commit are unreachable in production and untested. Mutations M9 (delete the readSelection non-finite guard, lines 57-59) and M10 (revert the applyComposerEdit isFinite clamps, lines 73-74) each leave all 43 unit+component tests green. A mounted <textarea> never reports a non-finite or null selectionStart, and grepping 14-voice/, extensions/text/ and DictationComposer.test.tsx finds no NaN/Infinity input anywhere; the only historical producer of a null selection was the e2e stub this same commit deleted (see the TEST-19 row). Not harmful - just defensive code presented as a fix with nothing behind it.

focusComposer's new generation-token guard is untested: mutation M7 (delete `if (isSuperseded(gen, requestGeneration)) return`) leaves all 43 unit+component tests green. The guard itself is correctly placed - the token is captured at call time and every caller (startRecording after its own ++, stopRecording under the stop token, cancelRecording after its ++) still matches at rAF time, so a normal successful stop DOES still restore the caret, confirmed by the 16/16 baseline. Worth recording only because the threat it names (an in-app A->B conversation switch) does not itself bump requestGeneration - cancelRecording early-returns when status is 'idle' - so the guard closes a one-animation-frame window rather than the scenario described in its comment.

NEW REGRESSION introduced by c096bb2d1. On the FIRST write of a session (session.span === null) resolveWriteSpan returns the RAW record-start anchor with no relocate/detach guard - that guard only exists once session.span is set. The new blank branch turns that unguarded span into an INSERTION of session.anchorText (previously it could only DELETE, which was harmless on a stale/clamped span). So a blank first decode - the common case, since the first ~1s of audio usually decodes to nothing - writes the user's own anchor word back over whatever now occupies those offsets. Oracle (component harness, real engine + real textarea): (P1) select 'Bob' in 'call Bob tomorrow', start recording, user CLEARS the composer, first interim decodes blank -> composer contains 'Bob'. Text the user deleted REAPPEARS. Same probe on c096bb2d1~1 leaves the composer '' - so this case was clean before this commit. (P2) user retypes 'call Carol tomorrow' -> 'call Bobol tomorrow' (parent produced the differently-corrupt 'call ol tomorrow'). A CARET anchor is unaffected (anchorText === '' makes restoreSpan an exact deletion). Fix direction: take the restore branch only when session.span is already set, or relocate the anchor against anchorText before the first write.

The nextSelection clamp added in this commit is LIVE production behaviour with NO test that could fail if it were reverted. Mutation M2 (`const span = raw`) leaves DictationComposer.test.tsx 20/20 green. A dedicated probe discriminates it in ONE tick: seed 'hello world' caret 11, start recording, user shortens the draft to 'hi' caret 2, one interim 'yes' -> clamped caret 6 (correct, follows the words), unclamped caret 2 (wrong, treated as 'entirely BEFORE the span'). The shipped suite misses it because a SECOND interim tick self-heals the caret (before is then inside the relocated span), and every existing test settles for TICK*2 or more. A single-tick assertion is what is missing. Note also the clamp is not the same normalization spliceTranscript/restoreSpan apply internally: normalizeSpan additionally orders start/end and widens off surrogate-pair boundaries, so on an astral-character boundary `edit` and the clamped `span` still differ by one and nextSelection's delta is off by one.

The `delivered` flag and the new 'Transcript discarded - the conversation was closed' announcement are LIVE with no test: mutation M3 (`const delivered = true`) leaves DictationComposer.test.tsx 20/20 green. No test in the file asserts `announcement` at all (the harness's `set` writes into a local object nothing reads). The logic itself is right for the normal cases - commitTranscript returns undefined ONLY when ownerTextStore is null, and the detached-session path still falls through to insertTranscript and returns a span - but it is wrong in one: when the pane closed AND the transcript was blank, a screen-reader user hears 'Transcript discarded' although there was nothing to discard; 'No speech detected' is the truthful message there. The ordering `!delivered ? discarded : text ? added : no-speech` makes the blank case unreachable whenever the pane is gone.

After a blank restore over a SELECTION anchor, session.written is set to the USER'S OWN word (anchorText) rather than to anything dictation wrote, so the session now claims ownership of user text for relocation purposes. Consequence: if that word occurs more than once in the draft and the recorded offsets go stale, relocateSpan's ambiguity check returns null and the session DETACHES - live captions silently stop for the rest of the recording. Oracle (P7): 'call Bob about Bob tomorrow' with the first 'Bob' selected, one blank decode, then the user types 'X ' at position 0, then a real decode 'Alice' -> nothing is written ('X call Bob about Bob tomorrow'). The parent commit instead corrupted ('X cal Alice l  about Bob tomorrow'), so this is the SAFE direction and arguably correct per DEC-5; recorded because it is a new, untested behaviour that a user experiences as dictation going dead mid-sentence.

commitTranscript's trailing-join-pad heuristic `const end = span.end - (session.written.endsWith(' ') ? 1 : 0)` now runs over a session.written that may be a RESTORE result rather than a splice result, because a blank FINAL transcript routes through the new restore branch. session.written is then anchorText, which has no join pad: if the user's original selection ended in a space, the returned caret lands one character to the LEFT of the restored text. No test covers a blank final transcript over a selection anchor.

MUTATION-COVERAGE RESULT for the four tests added in c096bb2d1 - all four are real, none passes for the wrong reason. (1) 'a blank interim over a SELECTION anchor puts the selected word back' is killed by M1 (blank branch -> spliceTranscript(value, span, transcript)). (2) 'dictation for a pane whose handle is gone writes nothing anywhere' is killed by M6 (ownerTextStore's `if (!handle) return null` -> `return Chat.$.TextStore`), AND it is NOT an idle control: instrumenting the mocked endpoints shows streamCalls=2 (interim ticks really fired) and finalCalls=1 (the final transcribe really ran) inside that test, so the write really was suppressed rather than never attempted. (3) 'applyComposerEdit reaches React onChange' is killed by BOTH M4 (prototype setter -> plain `el.value = text`, the exact no-op form that originally shipped) and M4b (drop the dispatchEvent). The round-3 fix is structurally incapable of doing what its comment claims, for the dominant case. resolveWriteSpan's header asserts 'the anchor is only honoured while it still holds exactly the text captured with it'. For a CARET anchor (no selection at record start - the common case) anchorText is '' and `value.slice(n,n) === ''` is true for EVERY in-range n, so the guard degrades to a bare bounds check and any replacement draft at least `anchor.end` long is accepted. Clamp-removal: the PRIMARY claim holds, a SECONDARY claim does not. I could not construct an out-of-range span from resolveWriteSpan: (a) relocateSpan's identity branch cannot return end>value.length (equality with a non-empty `written` forces end<=length); (b) its indexOf branch is in-range by construction; (c) its written==='' branch requires collapsed && start<=length; (d) an honoured anchor is bounds-checked at :242; (e) getSelection() and getText() read the SAME textarea instance with no await between them (composerAccess.ts:57,76), so the selection is always within the value read at :265. So the removed clamp WAS unreachable - claim proved, and mutation M10 (reinstating it) changes no test, consistent with that. However the accompanying 'One source of truth instead' claim is not delivered: nextSelection at :313 still receives `raw`, not the `normalizeSpan(value, raw)` that spliceTranscript actually spliced with, so a surrogate-boundary span still yields two different spans. Theoretical only (an anchor cannot land mid-surrogate through any reachable path I found); comment overclaim, not a defect.

R4 REGRESSION (INV-4 / DESIGN section 3 rule 5 - CANCEL DESTROYS USER TEXT). restoreDictation still splices `session.anchorText` - the text captured at RECORD START - over `session.span`. That is only correct if the session's FIRST write landed on the anchor, which is exactly the guarantee c9ce97760 deleted: resolveWriteSpan (:248) now writes at the composer's LIVE selection. The write target and the restore payload are now independent, and when they diverge cancel does not restore, it CORRUPTS. Oracle R5-P1 (component harness, real engine + real textarea): seed 'call Bob tomorrow' with 'Bob' selected (5,8), start recording, user re-selects 'tomorrow' (9,17), interim 'Alice' correctly lands there -> 'call Bob Alice', then CANCEL -> 'call Bob Bob'. The user's word 'tomorrow' is destroyed and 'Bob' is duplicated. Oracle R5-P2 (mirror case, anchorText==''): seed 'call Bob tomorrow' caret 0, user selects 'Bob' (5,8), interim 'Alice' -> 'call Alice tomorrow', CANCEL -> 'call  tomorrow' - the user's 'Bob' is deleted outright. BOTH probes PASS on the parent c9ce97760~1 (where stillHolds forced the first write onto the anchor, keeping target and payload paired) and FAIL on c9ce97760, so this is a regression introduced by this commit, not a pre-existing hole. FIX: capture the restore payload AT FIRST-WRITE TIME - when resolveWriteSpan returns the live selection for a session that owns no span, set session.anchor/anchorText from `value.slice(span.start, span.end)` before splicing. That makes restore correct by construction and keeps R5-P4/TEST-23 green.

The stated justification for deleting the `final` flag is falsified. The commit message argues the flag was 'a distinction with no observable difference' because 'the returned caret is what focusComposer applies'. focusComposer's apply is GUARDED by the generation token it was scheduled under (:172-179) and is DROPPED when superseded, so the returned caret is NOT always applied - and with the flag gone, `store.applyEdit` inside writeDictation now leaves the caret at nextSelection() (the user's own position) instead of after the transcript, so a skipped rAF leaves the wrong caret permanently. Previously applyEdit itself had already placed the final caret, making focusComposer redundant rather than load-bearing. Oracle R5-P5: seed 'draft here' caret 10, interim 'one', user parks the caret at 0, final 'one two', then a new startRecording in the same frame (bumps requestGeneration) -> caret 0 instead of 18; the next dictation therefore anchors at 0. PASSES on parent c9ce97760~1, FAILS on c9ce97760. Narrow (a ~1-frame click race, and the rAF-missing and pane-closed paths are both benign), hence low - but it is a real behaviour change, not the no-op the commit claims.
